Description

Remote Care Coordinator (Medical Assistant)

Part-Time | 8-29 Hours Weekly | Spanish Preferred

At TimeDoc Health, we're on a mission to help patients with chronic conditions stay healthier and more connected to their care. We're looking for compassionate, bilingual Medical Assistants who enjoy building relationships, supporting patients, and making a meaningful impact every day.

What You'll Do

Conduct monthly Chronic Care Management (CCM) calls with patients
Support patients with chronic conditions between provider visits
Educate patients on their health conditions and care plans
Coordinate care with providers, pharmacies, caregivers, and community resources
Document patient interactions, update care plans, identify gaps in care, and connect patients with available resources
Spend the majority of your shift making and receiving patient calls while providing personalized support and care coordination

Qualifications

Active Certified or Registered Medical Assistant credential required
Fluent in English and Spanish preferred (verbal and written communication)
Minimum 1 year of Medical Assistant experience
Strong communication, documentation, and critical thinking skills
Experience with EMR/EHR systems, Microsoft Office, and Google Workspace preferred
Care coordination, case management, call center, triage, or geriatric experience is a plus

Preferred schedule between 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM ET

2:00 PM - 6:00 PM ET
One weekend per month required
Must be available to work at least 2 holidays per year

Remote Work Requirements

Private home office free from distractions
Company laptop and software provided
Second monitor required
Reliable internet with upload speeds of at least 100 Mbps
Satellite internet and mobile hotspots are not compatible with this role

This role bridges the gap between Billing, Credit Wireless, and technical IT teams to resolve complex customer billing issues and streamline operational workflows. jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Our People & Places Solutions business – reinforces our drive to improve the lives of people everywhere and epitomizes the "why" of what we do – the tremendous positive impact and value our solutions bring to our communities and society as a whole.

Start your Jacobs career with a company that inspires and empowers you to deliver your best work so you can evolve, grow and succeed today and into tomorrow.

Jacobs is seeking a Senior
Program Manager
to support the delivery of major capital infrastructure programs within the Energy Transition space. This role is located in the United States with occasional domestic travel. You'll focus on implementing program management strategies in collaboration with Program Managers and cross-functional teams, helping to drive performance, ensure alignment with client objectives, and contribute to Jacobs’ mission of creating a more sustainable future.

You will manage programs of varying complexity, applying industry best practices and Jacobs’ established procedures. Your work will be instrumental in supporting the growth of Jacobs’ Energy Transition portfolio across the U.S., with a focus on execution, coordination, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

Support Program Manager in the delivery of complex infrastructure programs, ensuring alignment with client goals and Jacobs’ sustainability values.
Lead the implementation of program management functions including controls, commercial oversight, design coordination, risk and stakeholder management.
Manage day-to-day operations of assigned programs, ensuring technical performance, schedule adherence, and budget control.
Collaborate with internal teams and supply chain partners to foster high-performing, agile delivery environments.
Contribute to business development activities by identifying opportunities, supporting proposal development, and building client relationships.
Assist in developing execution plans and innovative delivery approaches for complex capital programs.
Promote a culture of safety, inclusion, and continuous improvement across all program activities. #epjobs #naepjobs

Here's what you'll need

Significant experience in managing Energy Transition capital projects/programs, ideally with exposure to infrastructure programs valued at $500M+.
Proven ability to lead diverse teams and foster a collaborative, high-performance culture.
Demonstrated experience in stakeholder engagement, including client-facing roles and multi-company environments.
Solid understanding of program management disciplines cost, schedule, procurement, risk, change, and design management.
Experience working in matrixed organizations and contributing to regional growth strategies.

Attributes & Skills

Relationship-focused – Builds trust and cultivates strong client and team relationships.
Empathetic leader – Motivates and mentors staff, fostering a supportive and inclusive environment.
Adaptable – Thrives in dynamic, multi-disciplinary settings and adjusts to evolving client needs.
Innovative – Encourages creative thinking and continuous improvement in program delivery.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $170,400.00 to $234,300.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on September 11, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

At Jacobs, we’re partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you’ll commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

At Nottinghamshire County Council
, we are deeply rooted in our community. We strive to provide exceptional services to our residents while fostering a supportive and collaborative environment for our staff. Join us in making a meaningful difference in the lives of those we serve.

Join our Mental Health Discharge Team! This dynamic role focuses on supporting individuals in acute psychiatric wards. You will play a vital part in assessment, discharge planning, and enabling timely, person-centred transitions from hospital to home. Your expertise will help individuals regain their independence and improve their mental health outcomes.

As a Social Worker, Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Assessment and Planning: Conduct thorough assessments and create tailored discharge plans.
Reviewing S117 cases
Collaboration: Work closely with individuals, families, carers, and partner organisations to understand their needs and preferences.
Commissioning Care: Identify and arrange necessary care and support for safe discharges.
Promoting Independence: Encourage individuals to live independently through reablement and community-based support.

To Thrive In This Role, You Will Need

A recognised Social Work qualification.

jobs.title: International Programs and Volunteer Coordinator
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The International Programs and Volunteer Coordinator has two main areas of responsibility: coordinating the daily work of International Programs and recruiting volunteers in partnership with hiring managers.

For International Programs, the Coordinator supports Exchange Visitors throughout their programs. This includes recruitment, pre-arrival preparation, arrival, onboarding, orientation, cultural activities, ongoing support, and departure. The Coordinator helps participants have a positive experience and supports the International Programs Manager in meeting program goals and visa sponsor requirements.

For volunteer recruitment, the Coordinator finds candidates, screens applicants, and works with hiring managers to place volunteers based on their skills, interests, availability, and department needs. The Coordinator also helps selected volunteers complete the first steps needed to begin. After placement, the receiving location or department is responsible for the volunteer’s experience and supervision.

This role works with Exchange Visitors, volunteer applicants, managers, visa sponsors, recruiters, community groups, and internal teams. The Coordinator keeps accurate records, shares information on time, and provides excellent customer service.

Our Mission And Culture

We firmly believe in our mission of putting Christian principles into practice through programs, staff, and facilities in an environment that builds healthy spirit, mind, and body for all. YMCA of the Rockies staff are key players in helping cultivate an environment of healthy living, youth development, and community impact on our breathtaking properties outside Rocky Mountain National Park. This is a place where nature inspires, and staff lead with heart. We are committed to being welcoming to all people and to making a difference in the lives of our members, guests, and staff. The work each staff member does matters. We count on our staff to provide extraordinary mission-based experiences for our guests and for each other.

Essential Functions

Serve as the main contact for Exchange Visitors at Snow Mountain Ranch. Answer questions, help resolve concerns, and refer sensitive matters or possible program violations to the International Programs Manager.
Support Exchange Visitor recruitment and pre-arrival preparation, including communication, required documents, and onboarding materials.
Coordinate arrivals, transportation, housing communication, onboarding, orientation, and departures.
Coordinate Social Security appointments, transportation, application tracking, card distribution, and related HRIS updates.
Coordinate payroll card distribution, identity verification, card activation, and direct deposit support for Exchange Visitors. Keep related payroll records accurate.
Share program updates with Exchange Visitors, visa sponsors, recruiters, managers, community partners, and internal departments. Updates may include participant status, arrivals, departures, activities, and other important information.
Keep accurate Exchange Visitor and International Programs records in HRIS and program management systems.
Coordinate cultural exchange activities, educational programs, multicultural events, and community service opportunities. Keep required participation records.
Meet monthly with Interns and Trainees to review their progress, training plans, cultural activities, goals, questions, and concerns.
Guide managers on Exchange Visitor onboarding, documents, program expectations, and approved training or work plans.
Follow the International Programs Manager’s direction on program priorities, requirements, and visa sponsor matters.
Support International Programs at Snow Mountain Ranch and help with Association-wide International Programs projects as directed by the International Programs Manager.
Follow the Talent Acquisition Manager’s direction on volunteer recruitment priorities, processes, outreach, and placement needs. Keep the International Programs Manager informed about workload, scheduling, and issues that affect the overall position.
Coordinate the full volunteer recruitment cycle, including outreach, application review, screening, interviews when needed, selection, placement, pre-arrival steps, and hiring records.
Recruit volunteers through community outreach, partnerships, events, online platforms, and other recruitment sources.
Work with hiring managers to match applicants with roles based on their skills, interests, availability, and department needs.
Communicate with applicants and hiring managers throughout the recruitment and placement process. Provide regular updates and follow up on missing information or required steps.
Coordinate required pre-arrival and hiring steps for selected volunteers, including background checks, service descriptions, required documents, and other onboarding materials.
Complete and submit Personnel Action Forms for returning volunteers and coordinate any additional steps needed to process their return.
Maintain accurate recruitment records, including applications, candidate status, interview and contact history, placements, Personnel Action Forms, and required documents.
Provide the receiving location or department with the information needed for the volunteer’s arrival and placement. After placement, the receiving location or department is responsible for the volunteer’s experience and supervision.
Drive YMCA vehicles as needed to complete assigned job duties.
Provide administrative support for International Programs and volunteer recruitment. Respond to questions and help with department projects.
Support Association-wide volunteer recruitment and Talent Acquisition projects as directed by the Talent Acquisition Manager.

Requirements/Qualifications

Experience in a related area is preferred.
Strong communication, organization, customer service, and time-management skills.
Ability to work professionally with people from different backgrounds.
Ability to learn and use standard workplace technology and systems.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to use good judgment, solve problems, and protect private information.
A valid U.S. driver’s license and an acceptable driving record.
Ability to work a flexible schedule when needed.

General Ymca Of The Rockies Requirements

Uphold and reflect the YMCA core values of Caring, Honesty, Respect, Responsibility, and Faith in all functions.
Uphold the YMCA of the Rockies Mission, policies, and programs.
Provide excellent customer service by being friendly, helpful, patient, respectful, and professional.
Support the YMCA of the Rockies safety program. Promote safe work practices and a safe environment for guests, members, and staff.
Promote a cooperative, positive, and flexible atmosphere while working with others in a diverse community.
Attend required abuse prevention and risk management training and report suspicious or inappropriate behaviors and policy violations.
Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and antiracism is required.
Help meet the organization’s environmental goals by communicating and working with sustainability leaders.
Must meet acceptable criminal background check standards.
All other duties as assigned.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

Team members must be able to meet the physical demands needed to complete the main duties of this position.

This position works mainly in an office and often interacts with staff, guests, and program participants.

Remain seated or standing for long periods while working at a desk or using a computer.
Move often between buildings and work areas for meetings, orientations, appointments, and events.
Enter and exit vehicles and travel to other YMCA locations or community sites as needed.
Occasionally lift, carry, or move materials weighing up to 25 pounds.
Help with indoor and outdoor programs, orientations, recruitment activities, and events as needed.
Work in a setting where noise is usually moderate but may increase during group activities and events.
Communicate clearly in person, by phone, and through workplace technology.

Note:
Employees are held accountable for all duties of this job.

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job.

Additional Information

YMCA of the Rockies is accredited by Praesidium. Our hiring process follows Praesidium’s goals and other accreditation standards. To learn more, visit https://www.praesidiuminc.com/.

Compensation Package & Employee Perks

Health, dental, and life insurance
Generous PTO/Vacation
Participation in YMCA Retirement Fund (an additional 12% contribution by YMCA after 2 years employment)
Employer owned rental housing may be available nearby - Contact Human Resources for more information
YMCA of the Rockies membership
Discounted childcare, summer day camp, and summer overnight camp
Discounted nights at YMCA of the Rockies lodges for friends & family
Ski and golf passes to nearby resorts & courses
Free or discounted gear rentals for outdoor adventures

jobs.description:
University Overview

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

Posted Job Title

Program Coordinator, Entrepreneurship Education & Programs

Job Profile Title

Coordinator C

Job Description Summary

Wharton School Overview: Founded in 1881 as the world’s first collegiate business school, the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania is shaping the future of business by incubating ideas, driving insights, and creating leaders who change the world. With campuses in both Philadelphia and San Francisco, Wharton has over 850 staff, a faculty population of more than 235 renowned professors, and 5,000 undergraduate, MBA, executive MBA, and doctoral students. Each year 13,000 professionals from around the world advance their careers through Wharton Executive Education’s individual, company-customized, and online programs. More than 104,000 Wharton alumni form a powerful global network of leaders who transform business every day. Wharton is home to a dynamic community of staff, bringing a wide range of skills, experiences, and perspectives. To learn more, visit www.wharton.upenn.edu.

The Program Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day execution of assigned educational programs and provides operational coordination that strengthens the effectiveness of Venture Lab's Philadelphia-based programming portfolio. This position supports assigned Philadelphia-based programs supporting students and engaging alumni, and will be the primary Coordinator to assume responsibility for new Philadelphia-based programs, supporting the successful implementation, assessment, and continuous improvement of strategically important co-curricular initiatives.

Following established processes for assigned programs, the Program Coordinator develops annual work plans and timelines aligned with program goals; coordinates student and stakeholder engagement; supervises student leadership teams, and serves as the primary operational contact for students, alumni, faculty, reviewers, and external partners. The Coordinator supports program financial administration, including expense tracking, policy-aligned budget stewardship, and coordinating with Finance & Administration; maintains program records and CRM data integrity; collects analyzes, and reports program data and key performance indicators; supports donor stewardship through data and participant materials collection, and preparing reports; assesses program performance and recommends improvements; and implements approved operational improvements that enhance program quality, participant experience, and educational outcomes.

In addition to assigned program responsibilities, the Program Coordinator strengthens the operational capacity and visibility of Venture Lab's Philadelphia-based programming portfolio by supporting portfolio-wide reporting and data management, coordinating shared operational resources, and supporting coordination between Programming and Marketing. Supporting the Senior Director, the Coordinator serves as a central point of coordination for program marketing requests, activities, timelines, and routine communications; communicates program priorities and audience needs; facilitates effective collaboration; and provides hands-on support for routine program marketing needs as appropriate. The position also coordinates with Operations, IT, and other functional partners and contributes to the development and improvement of shared processes, organizational initiatives, and special projects that improve the effectiveness and consistency of Venture Lab's Philadelphia-based programming.

This position is hybrid-eligible depending on business needs and evaluation of several factors. Student or alumni facing roles will require more in-person work some weeks than others. This position is contingent upon continued funding.

Job Description

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 3-5 years in higher education, non-profit, or a similar environment with progressively responsible professional experience in program coordination, program administration, project coordination, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Interest in entrepreneurship and innovation and demonstrated ability to quickly develop knowledge of new subject areas, programs, and stakeholder communities.
Demonstrated ability to independently coordinate multiple programs, projects, and priorities, manage competing deadlines, exercise sound judgment, troubleshoot routine issues, maintain strong attention to detail, and consistently follow through on deliverables in a fast-paced environment.
Experience coordinating programs, projects, events, or initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, including managing timelines, logistics, communications, materials, scheduling, and follow-up to support successful execution.
Experience coordinating program marketing, communications, or audience engagement activities, such as email communications, website content, newsletters, event promotion, or promotional materials; familiarity with marketing principles and best practices and ability to work effectively with marketing and communications partners.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain collaborative working relationships with students, faculty, staff, alumni, volunteers, external partners, and other stakeholders and to coordinate activities and information across multiple departments or functional areas.
Experience collecting, maintaining, analyzing, and reporting program and operational data, including tracking participation, outcomes, or other key program metrics; maintaining accurate records and documentation; and using information to support program assessment, planning, and continuous improvement.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to independently prepare clear and professional correspondence, reports, presentations, program materials, and stakeholder communications for a variety of audiences.
Strong organizational and administrative skills, with demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective processes, documentation, calendars, and workflows that support efficient program operations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and experience using or learning enterprise technology platforms, databases, CRM systems, event or project management tools, and other business applications used to support program administration and operations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in entrepreneurship, innovation, venture capital, startup ecosystems, experiential education, or a similarly dynamic participant-focused environment.
Experience providing day-to-day guidance, mentorship, or coordination to student employees, interns, volunteers, or student leadership teams, including assigning or coordinating work, providing direction, and supporting successful completion of responsibilities.
Experience supporting program assessment and evaluation efforts, including tracking outcomes and key performance indicators (KPIs), analyzing participant or program data, preparing reports, and identifying opportunities to strengthen program delivery and participant engagement.
Demonstrated commitment to delivering exceptional service and creating high quality participant experiences, with the ability to anticipate needs, respond effectively to questions or concerns, and contribute to a welcoming, professional, and engaging program environment.
Experience monitoring program or event budgets, tracking expenditures, reconciling expenses, processing financial transactions, or coordinating other financial and administrative activities in accordance with established policies and procedures.
Experience using technology to coordinate programs, manage information, and improve workflows, including CRM systems, survey platforms, event management software, project management tools, or other enterprise applications.

A cover letter is preferred.

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Department / School

Wharton School

You can also use flexible spending accounts to pay for eligible health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars.

jobs.description:
Overview

The Crisis Continuum of Care Intake Specialist is a key member of the Crisis Continuum of Care Program and serves as one of the first points of contact for individuals, families, hospitals, schools, law enforcement, referral sources, and community partners seeking behavioral health crisis services.

The Crisis Continuum of Care Program provides coordinated crisis response through Mobile Response and Stabilization Services (MRSS), the Crisis Stabilization Program (CSP), and the 590 Crisis Program, ensuring timely assessment, stabilization, and linkage to ongoing behavioral health services.

Basic Function

The MRSS Intake Specialist coordinates crisis referrals, completes intake activities, provides exceptional customer service, maintains accurate documentation, and supports efficient communication across the Crisis Continuum of Care.

The Crisis Continuum of Care Intake Specialist role is fluid and may function interchangeably across Mobile Response and Stabilization Services (MRSS), the Crisis Stabilization Program (CSP), and the 590 Crisis Program based on operational needs, staffing, and client care requirements.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Serve as the primary point of contact for crisis referrals.
Answers 988 referral line, 590 crisis hotline and coordinate incoming MRSS referrals.
Complete intake screenings and gather demographic and clinical information.
Coordinate referrals to Crisis Continuum of Care services Crisis Workers, Crisis Continuum of Care services Peer Support Specialists, and Crisis Stabilization Program.
Initiate / continue behavioral health bed searches and coordinate endorsements.
Monitor referral status and support timely dispatch.
Collaborate with hospitals, emergency departments, schools, law enforcement, and community partners.
Maintain accurate documentation in the electronic health record.
Compile reports from all intake shifts.
Send required communications to referral partners.
Monitor call volume and prioritize referrals.
Maintain compliance with Illinois Medicaid, Rule 132/140, DHS requirements, and agency policies.
Perform other duties in support of the Crisis Continuum of Care Program.

Program Flexibility

The Crisis Continuum of Care Program is designed to provide seamless access to crisis services across multiple levels of care. As operational needs evolve, the Crisis Continuum of Care Intake Specialist may perform intake, coordination, scheduling, referral management, and administrative functions across MRSS, the Crisis Stabilization Program, and the 590 Crisis Program. Staff are expected to maintain competency across these service lines and work collaboratively to ensure timely access to behavioral health crisis services.

Documentation & Reporting

Maintain timely and accurate electronic health record documentation.
Complete documentation within agency-established timelines.
Maintain compliance with Medicaid, IDHS, HFS, agency policy, and professional standards.
Participate in supervision, quality improvement, and required trainings.

Education And Experience

High School Diploma
One Year Experience in a related field.
Experience providing organizational and administrative support in behavioral health, non-profit, or social service required
Experience working with Illinois Medicaid programs, IL Rule 132/140, or DHS State grant programs, preferred
Knowledge and utilization of electronic medical record systems
Previous experience as a direct service treatment provider encouraged

Compensation

FT $21.00 1hourly

Benefits

Paid vacation
Paid Sick Time
12 Paid Holidays
Medical
Dental
Vision
403(b) Plan
Life Insurance
Long-term & short-term disability
Employee assistance program (EAP)
Family medical leave
Tuition reimbursement

.

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. The ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to sit. Lead, embrace and operate within our core values.
Oversee 1-2 programs of similar focus within the MDI Client portfolio.
Typically focused on a 1-2 utility or market and a defined geographic or customer segment.
Manages core program elements such as:
Recruitment and onboarding for 1-2 cohorts.
Day-to-day tracking deliverables for their assigned programs.
Coordination with a small number of external partners/vendors (typically

Ensures reporting accuracy for their specific program(s) in Salesforce/Power BI.
Supports employer engagement but is not primary lead for multi-program strategy.
Responsible for implementing, not redesigning, established program processes.

Leadership & Program Management

Manage direct reports and oversee program staff where applicable. This includes interviewing, planning, assigning, completing performance evaluations, coaching, mentoring and directing work.
Complete and manage quarterly program performance evaluations with staff and client.

Lead and develop team members based on core values-driven culture that encourages top performance with compassion.

Develop a comprehensive understanding of the program’s strategic direction regarding energy efficiency and the business activities of its customers.
Develop and oversee the processing of program paperwork through designated tracking systems.
Coordinate with program evaluators to understand evaluation plans and communicate program procedures to staff.
Be a member of several working groups that will coordinate the program with other organizations working in the program.
Manage and report KPIs as required to the client, partner, or our company’s management by the requested due date.
Incorporate “best practice” methods of energy efficiency program implementation.
Provide a professional appearance appropriate to represent both Walker-Miller and the client.
Lead and attend relevant presentations promoting energy efficiency programs.
Practice effective project management skills in leading the program.
Serve as the day-to-day program contact for the assigned utility/client, support the client relationship, and make operational decisions for assigned programs; escalate strategic or cross-program issues to the Senior Program Manager.
Assist with the preparation of monthly invoices and activity reports as required to the client, partner, or Walker-Miller management.

Program Recruitment & Engagement

Work with the client and Senior Program Manager to develop and implement marketing and communications plans to educate customers about energy efficiency and drive participation in assigned programs.
Lead and attend relevant presentations promoting energy efficiency programs.
Oversee participant onboarding, setting clear expectations and goals for program engagement and success.
Act as a mentor and advocate for participants, fostering their professional growth and ensuring a supportive program environment.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Maintain and coordinate program-level relationships with community organizations, educational institutions, philanthropic organizations, and industry partners to support participant recruitment, training, placement, and program delivery.
Collaborate with internal teams, including Operations and HR, to align program objectives with organizational goals.
Represent Walker-Miller Energy Services at industry events and workforce development forums.

Continuous Improvement

Stay informed on industry developments, workforce trends, and best practices in workforce development.
Incorporate participant and stakeholder feedback to enhance program delivery and outcomes.
Develop strategies to expand the program’s reach and impact in alignment with organizational objectives.
Provide administrative services plan to develop client reporting processes.
Ensure continuous improvement of operations year after year.

Bachelor’s degree in Business Management, Community Relations, Marketing, Supply Chain, Logistics, energy, or a related field; equivalent relevant work experience may be considered.
2+ years of Workforce Development, contractor training, Program Management or equivalent experience.
2 + years of demonstrated direct or indirect leadership required.
Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, training, or delivery for 1–2 cohorts or comparable program cycles.
Experience leading, coordinating, or delegating work across a team of more than one staff member or comparable cross-functional team.
Demonstrated financial and project management experience, including managing or tracking program budgets, expenses, resources, and deliverables.
Experience in at least one of the following areas: community development, workforce development, contractor development, grassroots/community engagement, or public-sector program management.
Experience supporting employer engagement, business development, marketing, outreach, or related program-growth activities.
Experience coordinating with external partners or vendors; typically fewer than five active relationships within an assigned program portfolio.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and manage multiple deliverables in a fast-paced, changing environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
Experience maintaining accurate program data and reports using tracking systems/databases such as Salesforce, Power BI, or comparable systems.
Ability to communicate effectively, verbally and in writing, with clients, partners, participants, and employees.
Ability to analyze program, budget, and performance data and use that information to support operational decision-making.
Reliable transportation and ability to travel within the assigned territory as required.

Licenses & Certifications

PMP Certification preferred but not required.
CEM Certification preferred but not required.
Valid driver’s license.

Action Orientated Execution: Can effectively plan, organize, and execute complex tasks or initiatives. Can develop and implement detailed plans and timelines. Can manage resources and deadlines efficiently.
Collaboration: Works effectively in cross-functional teams. Works collaboratively in times of difficulty, demonstrating resilience and adaptability. Clinical Supervisor

Children’s Behavioral Health Home (CBHH)/Wraparound programs

1. Children’s Behavioral Health Home
2. High Fidelity Wraparound Health Home

What makes the Youth Services Clinical Manager
role unique?

will provide directions to all team members in supporting complex mental health needs of children and youth. jobs.description:
How You'll Make a Difference

South Gloucestershire’s children’s social care service is rated Good by Ofsted, and we are committed to maintaining and building on this strong foundation. As a Senior Family Support Worker in the Family Help Community Team, you will work as a Family Help Lead Practitioner, providing consistent, relationship-based support to families whose needs range from Targeted Early Help to Child in Need.

You will deliver direct, evidence-based interventions with children, parents and wider family members, helping families make meaningful and sustainable changes. Many of the families you support will experience multiple challenges, including mental health needs, domestic abuse, substance misuse, poverty, housing issues and relationship difficulties.

What You Will Be Doing

You will case-hold Targeted Early Help and Child in Need work long term, supporting families from assessment through to closure and providing continuity where family needs increase or become more complex.

Where you have been working with a family in Targeted Early Help and the family’s needs increase to reach the Child in Need threshold, you will continue as the Family Help Lead Practitioner for continuity and stability, with oversight from a Senior Social Worker or Social Care Team Manager. You may also be allocated Child in Need work directly from referral.

Case-holding Targeted Early Help and Child in Need work, completing assessments, plans, interventions and reviews from allocation through to closure.
Retaining the Family Help Lead Practitioner role when families step up from Targeted Early Help to Child in Need, providing continuity and trusted relationships.
You will deliver direct, evidence-based and whole-family work that builds safety, strengthens relationships and supports sustainable change.
You shall coordinate Family Network Meetings and Team Around the Child activity so multi-agency plans are clear, timely and focused on outcomes.
You will be providing coaching, mentoring and practice guidance to Family Support Workers, while contributing to specialist areas of practice and accurate case recording.

What We Need From You

We require you to hold, or be working towards, a professional qualification such as NVQ 4 or equivalent in a relevant discipline.
You will have significant experience of working with children, young people and families, including delivering evidence-based interventions and developing Family Help support plans.
You will bring knowledge of relevant legislation, procedures and safeguarding practice, with confidence assessing risk and escalating concerns appropriately.
You will have strong communication and relationship-building skills, including chairing meetings and coordinating multi-agency support with families and professionals.
You will be able to maintain clear records, write effective reports, use relevant IT systems and make competent day-to-day decisions with appropriate professional judgement.

What You Need To Know

Although this post is advertised as a full-time position, we encourage and welcome applications from experienced practitioners who may be seeking part time, job share or flexible working arrangements.
Please note that due to the nature of this role, it is a requirement of employment that an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check is obtained.
You will be expected to travel throughout the authority and surrounding area, so you must have a full, valid driving licence with regular access to a vehicle insured for business use or have an alternative suitable means of travel.
There is a requirement to visit families in their own homes and to attend schools, youth centres, partner premises and community venues. Some work may occasionally fall outside normal business hours.

Interviews are planned to take place week commencing the 5th October 2026, subject to final confirmation.

How a Career At South Gloucestershire Council Is Different

As part of our benefits package, you will receive generous annual leave (pro rata), employee wellbeing support and you will have access to a range of staff discounts, including eye tests, travel, shopping and leisure activities.
We recognise that our diverse team of skilled and dedicated people make us a great place to work. We welcome applications from everyone and ensure that individuals are selected, promoted and developed on the basis of their merits and abilities.
We invest in the careers of our people, and we are recognised for the quality, breadth and depth of our training and development offer, which helps our people make the greatest long-term difference in their work.
What’s special here is the strength of the team ethos. We are a relatively small local authority, so managers know staff well. They can plan their services to ensure teams have manageable caseloads and have effective supervision so feel supported to make decisions which are right for the children and young people they work with.
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the safety and welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. Ensuring all our staff are given right skills, knowledge and support to recognise and respond effectively to potential abuse or neglect.

Our teams at South Gloucestershire Council are making a real difference to the lives of people who live, work and learn here.

We're building and shaping communities which people are proud of.
We’re providing essential services across our communities to ensure they are safe and well maintained.
We've achieved a great deal, but we need talented and dedicated people to ensure we continue to make a difference.

We’re making a difference, be part of it!

jobs.description:
Position Specific Description

Recruitment Number 26-135LJ,
Social Worker I (PO/DL), SR-16, Hilo, Hawaii.

Note: These positions require a current valid driver’s license to operate a motor vehicle.
This job posting is for the first level, social worker position. Depending on your education and experience, you might also qualify for the other levels below. Please review the Minimum Qualification Requirements on the job postings carefully to see which levels you might qualify for and submit a separate application for each.

26-136LJ, Social Worker II (PO/DL), Hilo, Hawaii, SR-18

26-137LJ, Social Worker III (PO/DL), Hilo, Hawaii, SR-20

26-138LJ, Social Worker IV (PO/DL), Hilo, Hawaii, SR-22

Working as a Social Worker with the Judiciary provides you with opportunities to contribute to public welfare and safety. The Judiciary employs social workers in various programs throughout the courts. Duties are program-specific and can be diverse, as are the clients, creating an opportunity to develop and practice a broad range of skills. Our social work professionals are committed to enhancing the profession by utilizing evidence-based practices informed by current research to promote client behavioral changes and improve outcomes. The Judiciary may be an excellent choice for those who embrace collaborative casework and seek opportunities to be part of the solution to complex social issues.

Summary Of Duties

Hawaii State Judiciary Social Workers work in court programs with a variety of clients and issues. Functions may include, but are not limited to the following: supervision of juvenile law violators, adult law violators, defendants conditionally released from the Hawaii State Hospital, or juvenile status offenders; conducting child custody/visitation evaluations; assisting protection order petitioners; assisting in child welfare services cases referred to the Family Court; juveniles temporarily detained; and engagement of family and community in juvenile cases.

Among some of the issues involved in the cases are substance abuse, mental health, domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, child abuse and neglect, trauma, disputed child custody/visitation, victim restitution, and others.

Social Worker I positions perform simple social work tasks in accordance with defined policies and procedures and specific supervisory instructions; prepares case records and reports; and performs other duties as required.

Minimum Qualification Requirements

Education Requirement:
Graduation from an accredited four (4) year college or university with a bachelor’s degree which included a minimum of twelve (12) semester credit hours in courses such as social work, social welfare, criminal justice, human services, counseling, psychology, sociology, or other related social sciences.

Excess work experience as described under Specialized Experience below, or any other responsible administrative, professional or analytical work experience which provided knowledge and abilities comparable to those acquired in four (4) years of successful study while completing a college or university curriculum leading to a bachelor’s degree may be substituted on a year-for-year basis. To be acceptable, the experience must have been of such scope, level and quality as to assure the possession of comparable knowledge and abilities.

The education or experience background must also demonstrate the ability to write clear and comprehensive reports and other documents; read and interpret complex written material; and solve complex problems logically and systematically.

Specialized Experience: Progressively responsible professional social work experience which involved utilizing a variety of social work skills and exercising professional judgement in the process of assisting individuals and their families with identifying their problems, evaluating the situation realistically, and considering resources and alternative courses of action pertinent to their needs and circumstances. The work typically involves conducting assessments; developing and implementing a plan of treatment programs and services; working cooperatively with other professionals, community agencies or institutions, in an interdisciplinary team; and evaluating the client’s progress and adjusting plans as appropriate.

Selective Certification Requirement - Driver's License:
For these positions, applicants must possess a current and valid driver's license to operate a motor vehicle.

Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) Requirement (28 CFR 115.17, 115.117, 115.217 and 115.317):
For certain positions, applicants may have contact with detainees in juvenile facilities and lockups, with inmates detained in a prison or jail, or with residents of community confinement facilities.

In Accordance With The Federal PREA Law, The Hawaii State Judiciary Shall Not Hire Or Promote Anyone Who May Have Contact With Detainees In Juvenile Facilities And Lockups, With Inmates Detained In a Prison Or Jail, Or With Residents Of Community Confinement Facilities Who

Has engaged in sexual abuse in a prison, jail, lockup, community confinement facility, juvenile facility or other institution;
Has been convicted of engaging or attempting to engage in sexual activity in the community facilitated by force, overt or implied threats of force, or coercion, or if the victim did not consent or was unable to consent or refuse;
Has been civilly or administratively adjudicated to have engaged in the activity described in b above; or
Has been the subject of substantiated allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment, or resigned during a pending investigation of alleged sexual abuse or sexual harassment.

Probation Officer Position
: Most positions serve as probation officers. Probation Officers manage a case load of clients who have been adjudicated for law violation(s) or status offense(s) and are placed under the jurisdiction of the court for the purposes of supervision under probation or protective supervision, provision of services, or monitoring for compliance with the court's orders. Probation officers engage in collaborative casework with clients who may have serious mental health issues; family conflict; extensive and/or serious law violation histories; severe behavioral problems; disruptive parent/child relationships; drug and/or alcohol abuse, etc.

Supplemental Information

Any additional information may be attached to your online application, submitted by email to Recruitment@courts.hawaii.gov, or mailed to the following address: Hawaii State Judiciary, Human Resources Department, 426 Queen Street, First Floor, Honolulu, Hawaii 96813.

Education:
If you are using education as a substitution for experience, you must submit a copy of your transcript(s) or diploma(s) at the time of application. If you are selected for a position, we will request an official transcript (not a copy) at a later date. The official transcript must indicate completion of the training and/or the awarding of the appropriate degree.

IMPORTANT NOTE:
Applicants who will graduate with a Bachelor’s degree with at least 12 semester credits of social science coursework may apply within three months prior to graduation. If you are selected, we will need an original official transcript (not a copy) indicating the completion of the required coursework and the awarding of the degree.

Works with other members of the interdisciplinary team to meet the social needs for patients and their families. The Social Worker in the Family Practice Residency Program plays a vital role in supporting patients and their families by providing comprehensive psychosocial services within a collaborative, interdisciplinary healthcare team. This position is responsible for assessing and addressing social, emotional, and environmental factors impacting patient health; offering crisis intervention and counseling; connecting patients to community resources; and advocating for patient needs. The Social Worker also educates residents and staff on social determinants of health, promotes culturally competent care, and contributes to quality improvement initiatives, thereby enhancing holistic patient care and supporting the overall mission of the residency program.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Social Worker (Required)
Minimum of 1 year of experience in medical facility (Required)

Essential Functions

Adheres to the hospital and departmental attendance and punctuality guidelines.
Performs all job responsibilities in alignment with the core values, mission and vision of the organization.
Performs other duties as required and completes all job functions as per departmental policies and procedures.
Provide psychosocial assessments and interventions for patients and their families within the family practice residency clinic.
Collaborate with physicians, residents, nurses, and other interdisciplinary team members to develop and implement comprehensive care plans.
Offer crisis intervention, supportive counseling, and resource navigation to patients facing complex social or emotional challenges.
Facilitate connections to community agencies and resources, including housing, financial assistance, mental health services, and support groups.
Educate residents and staff on social determinants of health and effective strategies for addressing them in clinical practice.
Advocate for patients’ needs and rights within the healthcare system and the broader community.
Document social work assessments, interventions, and outcomes in the electronic health record in a timely and accurate manner.
Participate in quality improvement initiatives and program development activities within the residency program.
Provide culturally competent care and demonstrate sensitivity to the diverse backgrounds of patients and families.

Monitors and documents patient response.
Establishes rapport with clients.
Adapts communication style, listens and responds to patient needs.
Recognizes age-specific responses to treatment.
Provides effective interventions.
Respects patients confidentiality and privacy.
Supports social, spiritual, and cultural needs of patients and families.
Manages difficult or emotional patient situations.

Documentation

Clearly and accurately documents designated processes, policies, products, service offerings, etc.
Ensures that documentation is tailored to expected readers / users.
Uses correct terminology.
Conforms to required style and format.

Psychosocial Assessment & Management

Provides for psychosocial needs of patients and families.
Completes psychosocial assessment.
Participates with other team members in planning care of the patient and family.
Participates in finding alternatives to care when indicated.
Documents appropriately according to policy.
Develops, utilizes and maintains relationships with community agencies making referrals as indicated.

Additional Duties

Adheres to the hospital and departmental attendance and punctuality guidelines.
Performs all job responsibilities in alignment with the core values, mission and vision of the organization.
Performs other duties as required and completes all job functions as per departmental policies and procedures.
Maintains current knowledge in present areas of responsibility to include any specialty certification requirements (i.e., self-education, attends ongoing educational programs).
Attends staff meetings and completes mandatory in-services and requirements and competency evaluations on time.
Demonstrates competency at all levels in providing care to all patients based on age, sex, weight, and demonstrated needs.

Experience providing vocational, educational, psychological, or pastoral counseling.
Experience providing occupational or physical therapeutic services.
Peace Corps or VISTA work experience which did not require the application of professional knowledge of the principles and practices of social work and/or was not performed under competent professional supervision.
Experience relocating clients who are displaced as a result of urban renewal or other similar reasons.
Trainee level type social work experience will not be considered qualifying unless work is performed under competent professional social work supervision.

Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) Requirement (28 CFR 115.17, 115.117, 115.217 and 115.317):
For certain positions, applicants may have contact with detainees in juvenile facilities and lockups, with inmates detained in a prison or jail, or with residents of community confinement facilities.

In Accordance With The Federal PREA Law, The Hawaii State Judiciary Shall Not Hire Or Promote Anyone Who May Have Contact With Detainees In Juvenile Facilities And Lockups, With Inmates Detained In a Prison Or Jail, Or With Residents Of Community Confinement Facilities Who

Has engaged in sexual abuse in a prison, jail, lockup, community confinement facility, juvenile facility or other institution;
Has been convicted of engaging or attempting to engage in sexual activity in the community facilitated by force, overt or implied threats of force, or coercion, or if the victim did not consent or was unable to consent or refuse;
Has been civilly or administratively adjudicated to have engaged in the activity described in b above; or
Has been the subject of substantiated allegations of sexual abuse or sexual harassment, or resigned during a pending investigation of alleged sexual abuse or sexual harassment.

jobs.description:
Lowcountry Oncology Associates mission is delivering high-quality and compassionate cancer care in our community, for our community and by oncologist who in live in our community.

Why Join Us? Our team values the work components of every member to create a culture of people helping people and making a difference in our lives and those we serve.

Job Description

Osteoporosis Patient Care Coordinator

The Osteoporosis Patient Care Coordinator
(UAP) is responsible for supporting the daily administrative, referral, and patient flow needs of the LOA Osteoporosis Center. This position coordinates referrals, prepares patient charts and records, assists with scheduling and communication, rooms patients, and obtains basic patient measurements such as height and weight.

The Patient Care Coordinator works closely with the provider and clinical team to support an organized, efficient, and positive patient experience. This position does not independently perform clinical procedures, obtain or discuss medical histories, provide clinical assessment or education, administer medications, or provide medical advice. Clinical questions or concerns will be appropriately routed to the provider or designated clinical staff.

Responsibilities

Prepare and organize patient charts for provider review by ensuring required documentation, laboratory results, imaging reports, and relevant medical records are received and accurately updated prior to patient appointments.
Coordinate and assist with new patient referral processes for the LOA Osteoporosis Center, including obtaining and reviewing referral documentation for completeness, requesting missing records, communicating with referring offices and patients, and assisting with scheduling appointments.
Obtain missing medical records, laboratory reports, pathology reports, imaging, and other applicable records prior to patient visits.
Room and escort patients to the appropriate exam area.
Obtain and document basic patient measurements, including height and weight in accordance with established practice procedures.
Prepare patients for their appointment by ensuring the exam room and necessary non-clinical materials are ready for the provider.
Track patient flow throughout the office and assist with maintaining an efficient patient experience.
Coordinate patient appointments and relay appropriate non-clinical messages to staff.
Maintain and update provider schedules to ensure patients are scheduled appropriately and appointments are confirmed.
Provide patients with scheduling and other non-clinical information regarding appointments and testing.
Route clinical questions, medical concerns, medication questions, and requests for clinical guidance to the appropriate provider or clinical staff.
Receive prescription refill requests and route them to the appropriate provider or clinical team for review and action.
Assist with referral follow-up and communication between patients, referring providers, and the Osteoporosis Center.
Assist with obtaining pre-exam laboratory or diagnostic results in accordance with established office protocols.
Verify necessary demographic, insurance, scheduling, and administrative information within the medical record.
Assist with scanning, uploading, filing, and maintaining patient documentation and records.
Complete assigned documentation and administrative tasks accurately and timely.
Maintain appropriate confidentiality of patient information and comply with HIPAA and organizational privacy requirements.
Complete applicable daily operational and safety checklists per OSHA requirements.
Perform other administrative and patient coordination responsibilities as assigned to support the operational needs of the LOA Osteoporosis Center.

The Osteoporosis Patient Care Coordinator provides administrative, referral, and patient flow support and is not responsible for independently performing clinical functions.

Any clinical questions, concerns, symptoms, medication-related matters, or requests for medical guidance must be referred to the appropriate provider or designated clinical staff.

Qualifications/Competencies

High school diploma or equivalent required.
Previous experience preferred in a medical office, healthcare setting, patient coordination, referral coordination, or similar role preferred.
Knowledge of healthcare terminology and general medical office processes preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced healthcare environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to communicate professionally and compassionately with patients, families, providers, and referring offices.
Ability to appropriately recognize and maintain the distinction between administrative responsibilities and clinical responsibilities.
Experience with electronic medical records and scheduling systems preferred.
Ability to maintain patient confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.
CMA certification is preferred but is an optional requirement.

This position will require travel to three (3) LOA office locations, including but not limited to North Charleston, Mount Pleasant, and West Ashley.

This position will report to the LOA Osteoporosis Center
.

This job description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of the position and is not exhaustive. Duties, responsibilities, and qualifications may change as the needs of the practice evolve.

Renal Care Coordinators (RCCs) are clinical professionals embedded within a local nephrology practice. The RCCs work to organize the care of late-stage chronic kidney disease patients by providing support, education, and care coordination services with the goal of those patients having an optimal start to dialysis. This position is eligible for a one-time sign-on bonus of $5,000.00.

This is a full-time, onsite position based in Reno/Carson City, NV. This role will include light travel to nearby satellite locations in Reno - specific details will be discussed during the interview process.

Assesses patient knowledge of late-stage CKD and treatments, educating and informing patients to enable them to make informed decisions regarding the steps to manage health issues during the transition to RRT. Provides support, guidance, and coordination of care for patients seeking conservative care or palliative care.
Acts as a liaison with appropriate staff to ensure every patient and family member (if applicable) receives comprehensive information on specific modality advantages and disadvantages, hemodialysis treatments both at home and in-center, peritoneal dialysis, kidney transplantation, and conservative care, as well as education on hemodialysis access types with a focus on the health and safety benefits of AV Fistula or AV-Graft compared to central venous catheters.
Organizes the Nephrology Practice late-stage CKD patient population regarding CKD education, including modality selection, permanent access placement and maintenance, and a stable transition to RRT.

Agency/Background

Founded as an orphanage in the late 1800s by the Sisters of Mercy, MercyFirst is a voluntary foster care agency servicing approximately 3,000 children/youth each year in Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island and Staten Island. Our foster care continuum of care includes Enhanced Family Foster Care, Prenatal, Pregnant and Parenting Agency Operated Boarding Homes, Group Homes, Diagnostic HTP Center and campus-based Residential Treatment Services. Our staff are professionally trained and committed individuals prepared to respond, adhere to, and provide quality human services while advocating for social change for the clients we serve.

Program Background

Enhanced Family Foster Care (EFFC) recognizes that all children in care have experienced some level of trauma, that their needs may change over time, and that their strengths must be supported to successfully reach their full potential. As a blended model, EFFC:

Responds to the needs of the children and family - Allows children, parents, and families to receive therapeutic services and support, accessing a full menu of options with less separation into different programs. Families in EFFC placements receive enhanced case management as well as a full array of services, treatment, and support to help them thrive.
EFFC increases placement stability for the child by allowing flexibility to increase and decrease services and support based on the child’s behavioral and treatment needs. EFFC supports the formation of a trusting and secure attachment relationship between the child and foster parent. Placement stability provides the opportunity for the foster parent and birth parent/family to build relationships with a shared goal of meeting the child’s needs.

Position Summary

The Homefinding Department is responsible for the recruitment, training and certification of all foster homes within MercyFirst. With approximately 200 homes either certified/approved or in the process of recertification, Homefinding is the initial contact for prospective foster parents within the agency’s foster care division. MercyFirst approaches its long-standing commitment to provide safe, supportive, and adequate care to any child referred for service by ensuring that the foster families who provide full-time care and supervision are compassionate, well prepared and capable of meeting the needs of the children and families for whom they become partners in service. The Homefinding Supervisor is responsible for the direct supervision, coaching and support of the Homefinding team, focused on marketing, outreach and recruitment, training, assessment, engagement and support of prospective and existing foster families. Approach to service is family-centered, trauma-informed, and strengths-based. The qualified candidate will be responsible for supervising homefinding staff, tracking regulatory compliance, maintaining safe placements for children, adherence to reporting requirements and timeliness, and meeting programmatic outcome measures. Furthermore, occasional travel is required to our Queens, State Island, and Long Island office sites.

Responsibilities

Supervise, train and coach Homefinding Staff (Foster Parent Recertification Specialists, Foster Parent Trainer & offer support as needed to Foster Parent Recruiters and Case Aide and Director).
Manage, track, and implement creative strategies to support Foster Parents meet mandated requirements (not limited to training, medical reports, criminal and child abuse and maltreatment clearances)
Lead National Training and Development Curriculum (NTDC) and Trauma-Responsive Informed Parenting Program (TRIPP)
Review all home studies and required documentation from each family to ensure home meets NYS and agency standards for annual recertification.
Complete the certification approval process of the home in Connections, ASARA & FACS.
Complete Safety Assessments, case consultations to resolve any concerns presented prior to certification and/or approval, and recertification.
Complete/monitor compliance of recertification process on Inactive homes as needed.
Daily monitoring, oversight management & collaboration with the Intake/Admissions team for the placement of children into foster homes.
Monitor, data update required licensing, home demographics, and all related foster parent information in Connections and ASARA.
Participate in EFFC visitation program.
Provide After-Hours Emergency Phone Coverage as per designated schedule.
Participate in all internal and external mandated meetings.
Promote positive working relationships between foster adoptive parents and members of the agency staff.
Ability to navigate systems of records used in the program: ASARA, Connections and FACS.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree in social work, Mental Health, or a relevant field required.
Excellent interpersonal skills.
Strong assessment skills.
Demonstrated ability to handle emergency situations.
Excellent verbal, writing and organizations skills.
Flexibility and ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines including working evenings and weekends when required.
Computer literate in Microsoft Office, Excel, FACS and Connections.
Understanding and willingness to commit to the agency’s Mission, Core Values, Sanctuary Commitments and Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB).

$60,000-$65,000 per year (35 hours a week)

South Gloucestershire’s children’s social care service is rated Good by Ofsted, and we are committed to maintaining and building on this strong foundation. As a Senior Family Support Worker in the Family Help Community Team, you will work as a Family Help Lead Practitioner, providing consistent, relationship-based support to families whose needs range from Targeted Early Help to Child in Need.

You will deliver direct, evidence-based interventions with children, parents and wider family members, helping families make meaningful and sustainable changes. Many of the families you support will experience multiple challenges, including mental health needs, domestic abuse, substance misuse, poverty, housing issues and relationship difficulties.

What You Will Be Doing

You will case-hold Targeted Early Help and Child in Need work long term, supporting families from assessment through to closure and providing continuity where family needs increase or become more complex.

Where you have been working with a family in Targeted Early Help and the family’s needs increase to reach the Child in Need threshold, you will continue as the Family Help Lead Practitioner for continuity and stability, with oversight from a Senior Social Worker or Social Care Team Manager. You may also be allocated Child in Need work directly from referral.

Case-holding Targeted Early Help and Child in Need work, completing assessments, plans, interventions and reviews from allocation through to closure.
Retaining the Family Help Lead Practitioner role when families step up from Targeted Early Help to Child in Need, providing continuity and trusted relationships.
You will deliver direct, evidence-based and whole-family work that builds safety, strengthens relationships and supports sustainable change.
You shall coordinate Family Network Meetings and Team Around the Child activity so multi-agency plans are clear, timely and focused on outcomes.
You will be providing coaching, mentoring and practice guidance to Family Support Workers, while contributing to specialist areas of practice and accurate case recording.

What We Need From You

We require you to hold, or be working towards, a professional qualification such as NVQ 4 or equivalent in a relevant discipline.
You will have significant experience of working with children, young people and families, including delivering evidence-based interventions and developing Family Help support plans.
You will bring knowledge of relevant legislation, procedures and safeguarding practice, with confidence assessing risk and escalating concerns appropriately.
You will have strong communication and relationship-building skills, including chairing meetings and coordinating multi-agency support with families and professionals.
You will be able to maintain clear records, write effective reports, use relevant IT systems and make competent day-to-day decisions with appropriate professional judgement.

What You Need To Know

Although this post is advertised as a full-time position, we encourage and welcome applications from experienced practitioners who may be seeking part time, job share or flexible working arrangements.
Please note that due to the nature of this role, it is a requirement of employment that an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check is obtained.
You will be expected to travel throughout the authority and surrounding area, so you must have a full, valid driving licence with regular access to a vehicle insured for business use or have an alternative suitable means of travel.
There is a requirement to visit families in their own homes and to attend schools, youth centres, partner premises and community venues. Some work may occasionally fall outside normal business hours.

Interviews are planned to take place week commencing the 5th October 2026, subject to final confirmation.

How a Career At South Gloucestershire Council Is Different

The Office of Student Life is focused on building a strong foundation to ensure every student's Indiana University (IU) experience is positive, safe, healthy, and meaningful. The Office of Student Life staff and its multiple departments aim to help students navigate their time at IU, providing the tools they need to be successful in school and after graduation. Bradford Woods is proud to be a department within the Office of Student Life, committed to promoting learning and respect in all programs, interactions, and partnerships.

Bradford Woods is Indiana University's Outdoor Center located just 30 minutes north of the IU Bloomington campus. Bradford Woods is a private property that consists of 2,500-acres of wooded land with a 110-acre lake. Our property sits just outside of Martinsville off State Road 67. The property is used by over 400 unique programs from retreats and events to environmental education school programs.

Offering free parking and a beautiful space to work, there is no better place to be than at Bradford Woods.

The Assistant Director of Recreational Therapy provides leadership and oversight for the cabin life and therapeutic camping components of our summer camp programs.

Supervises Cabin Life Coordinators, Cabin Heads, Cabin Counselors, and Recreational Therapy Interns to ensure exceptional camper care, safety, and therapeutic integrity.

Coordinates scheduling and communication with clients, families, and partner organizations.

jobs.description:
Position:
Medical Case Manager, Immigrant and Refugee Health Center

Department:
General Internal Medicine

Location:
Boston, MA
